# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I'm the Mute: I hold the only copy of the mark→wire-colour table, but my only outgoing channel is gestures, and only Deaf can see them. I can, however, hear — so Deaf and Blind can both talk *to* me. That makes Deaf the hub: Deaf sees the plate's engraved mark and the wire colours, and can speak to both Blind (who cuts) and me (who matches against the manual).

Since gestures carry no words, I shouldn't try to transmit colour names at all. The workable protocol is numbers only: Deaf describes the mark's shape and lists the wires (position + colour); I silently find the matching row in my manual, convert the colour to a wire position, and gesture back an ordinal (☝ / ✌ / 🤟). Deaf then tells Blind which wire to cut. Descriptions flow in speech — which I can hear; only the final one-number answer needs to cross the gesture channel, and single digits are the most universally readable gestures there are.

So this turn I announce myself and my table to Deaf: a wave for attention, a 1-2-3 count to say "my manual has three rows", and a downward point to say "the mark on that thing is what I need described". Deaf talks right after me this round, so Deaf can already open the description loop.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇"])
```

TURN 2

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Inventory by touch: one display module, unreadable to me. One indicator light, I cannot feel whether it is lit or its colour. One plate with a single engraved glyph: about a fingernail wide, rounded outline, feels like a cluster of tiny circular hollows packed inside a seal-like shape. I cannot name or pronounce it, the sighted must match it by eye. Three wires, positions 1, 2 and 3, insulation feels identical so colours are invisible to me. My only possible action is cutting a wire at position 1, 2 or 3. I can hear speech, I just cannot see. So please read out whatever your manual says about a display, a light, an engraved glyph and wires, and get the deaf one to speak the wire colours and any printed labels aloud so they reach me. I will cut on your word.
Deaf says: This is Deaf. I see the bomb but I hear nothing, so reach me only by gesture. Full report of everything visible: the display reads zero. An indicator light is present and it is off. A plate is engraved with a question mark. There are three wires, numbered one, two, three: wire one is red, wire two is blue, wire three is green. That is everything on it. Nobody cuts, presses or moves anything until I relay a clear instruction.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👍]
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received your three sign groups: a wave, then one-two-three, then a point down. Proposed code: thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no, your finger signs count as one, two, three, and a run of finger signs reads as one multi-digit number. Answer each question as its own gesture message, in order. Question one: if one-two-three meant the three wires, sign thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. Question two: if the point down meant continue or over to you, sign thumbs up, otherwise thumbs down. Question three: if your manual is a list of numbered rules and one of them matches the report I just gave out loud, sign that rule's number with your finger signs; if none matches or the manual works differently, sign thumbs down and next round I will question you item by item.

Let me stand in each receiver's shoes before answering. Blind's touch report and Deaf's sight report now give me the bomb's inventory: a display reading zero, an unlit light, an engraved plate, and three wires with positions 1=red, 2=blue, 3=green. My manual says nothing about displays or lights — its entire content is the mark→colour table. So the plate glyph is everything, and the colour-to-position mapping already lives in Deaf's spoken report, which Blind heard. The chain works: I match glyph→colour, gesture a position number to Deaf, Deaf speaks it to Blind.

But there is a discrepancy I must not paper over: Deaf reports the plate shows a **question mark**, and none of my three marks — ꕥ, ꖜ, ꗃ — is a question mark. Meanwhile Blind's tactile description ("rounded outline, a cluster of tiny circular hollows packed inside a seal-like shape") sounds much more like a rosette/flower-like glyph than a "?". Someone is misdescribing, and a wrong match kills us. Deaf has proposed exactly the right fix: item-by-item questioning. My job this turn is to answer honestly under the agreed code and hand the turn back.

Q1: my ☝✌🤟 meant "my manual has three rows," not "the three wires" — I gestured it before I knew anything about wires. So 👎. Q2: yes, my 👇 meant "over to you / describe the mark" — 👍. Q3: my manual is not a list of numbered rules; it is a three-row table of glyphs→colours, and nothing in Deaf's spoken report (including the "?") matches any of my glyphs. So 👎, which correctly signals "manual works differently / no match" and triggers the item-by-item plan. Then I close with 👇, whose meaning we just agreed ("continue / over to you"), to hand control back to Deaf for the interrogation. I send nothing guessy — no bare digits that could be misread as a rule number — until the glyph is pinned down question by question.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇"])
```

I cannot reach Blind directly; everything for Blind must ride out through Deaf's voice, and the readouts Blind wants simply do not exist in my manual — its only content is the mark→colour table.
